correctness.rationale: For ellipsoid E(c,Q) containing the closed ball B_r(0) strictly, let s(u)=u^TQu, y(u)=u·c, D=det Q. Affine hyperplane slicing gives V(u)=κ_{n-1}√D [s(u)-(r-y(u))²]^{(n-1)/2}/s(u)^{n/2}, radicand strictly positive. Raise to 2/(n-1); odd part under u↦-u is 4r D^{1/(n-1)} y/s^{n/(n-1)}. If one center vanishes equality forces both to vanish. For two nonzero centers, homogenize odd equality, raise to n-1 and apply UFD to the positive-definite real quadratic forms in n>=3, irreducible there, to force Q'=λQ; the unpowered odd formula forces c'=c. Even part then forces λ=1. For centered nonspherical Q, homogeneity and irreducibility of s and s-r²||x||² likewise force Q'=λQ and λ=1; for Q scalar the transformed data are constant and the only way Q' can have constant t↦(t-r²)t^{-n/(n-1)} on its Rayleigh interval is Q' scalar, with identical radius. These exhaust all centers and shapes. Dimension n>=3 is essential to irreducibility; no n=2 claim. Finite numerical checks do not replace polynomial factorization.

value.rationale: Determination of a general ellipsoid from noncentral supporting-ball sections is a natural exact inverse problem inside the longstanding Barker--Larman question. Unlike centered or perturbative cases it simultaneously identifies arbitrary translation, orientations and principal semiaxes, proving a sharp global injectivity benchmark for geometric tomography.
